final_candidates.decision_summary: Lowest ProteinMPNN compatibility (z=0.033) and zero mutant frequency in MSA indicate strong disruption of a highly conserved position — burying a charged Asp is strongly destabilizing.
Proline at a buried, conserved Phe is strongly backbone-incompatible (z=0.101) and never observed in homologs, predicting fold disruption.
Very poor structural compatibility (z=0.107) at a conserved hydrophobic position supports a destabilizing proline insertion that breaks local secondary structure.

stop_reason.detail: Converged ranking: top candidates have consistent, strongly negative structural and evolutionary evidence for fold disruption, and alternatives were rejected as tolerated.

history.rationale: Trp17 is a large aromatic likely buried in the PsaE core; proline substitution breaks local secondary structure and removes favorable packing, strongly destabilizing the fold.
Proline substitution of a buried aromatic Trp strongly disrupts local backbone geometry and hydrophobic packing; best folding-disruption candidate.
Loss of the conserved aromatic Trp plus proline is chemically disruptive and never seen evolutionarily, though MPNN penalizes it only moderately (z=0.358).
Leu11 lies in a hydrophobic N-terminal segment; proline introduces backbone rigidity and loses a hydrogen-bond donor, disrupting helix/strand formation.
Leu-to-Pro in an early hydrophobic segment breaks helix/strand propensity and destabilizes the N-terminal core.
Very poor structural compatibility (z=0.107) at a conserved hydrophobic position supports a destabilizing proline insertion.
Phe48 is a conserved aromatic likely packed in the core; replacing it with proline both removes hydrophobic packing and distorts the backbone.
Phe-to-Pro removes a bulky aromatic core residue and introduces a backbone kink, likely destabilizing.
High structural compatibility (z=0.780) and low MSA applicability (0.465) indicate the site tolerates proline; unlikely to destabilize.

rejection.reason: High structural compatibility (z=0.780) and low MSA applicability (0.465) indicate the site tolerates proline; unlikely to destabilize.

history.rationale: Ile33 sits in a hydrophobic stretch (I-I-Y-P-V-I-V); proline substitution should kink or break this region and destabilize folding.
Ile-to-Pro adjacent to the existing P35 likely disrupts the local turn/loop structure.
MPNN says proline is favorable here (z=0.912) and 17% of homologs already carry Pro — this mutation is tolerated, not disruptive.

rejection.reason: MPNN says proline is favorable here (z=0.912) and 17% of homologs already carry Pro — this mutation is tolerated, not disruptive.

history.rationale: Removing the bulky Trp17 side chain and replacing with glycine creates a large cavity in the core, destabilizing the hydrophobic core.
Glycine at the buried Trp increases conformational entropy and removes core packing; strong alternative to W17P.
Removing the bulky Trp side chain destabilizes packing, but MPNN tolerance is moderate so it ranks below the proline hits.
Phe40 is an aromatic residue in a likely structured region; proline substitution disrupts packing and local backbone geometry.
Aromatic-to-Pro substitution in the central region should impair packing.
Proline substitution at a buried Phe is strongly backbone-incompatible (z=0.101) and never observed in homologs, predicting fold disruption.
Val24 is a hydrophobic core candidate; introducing a charged Asp into the core creates a buried unsatisfied charge, strongly destabilizing.
Buried hydrophobe-to-charged mutation is a classic destabilizer.
Lowest ProteinMPNN compatibility (z=0.033) on the experimental backbone and zero mutant frequency in MSA indicate strong disruption of a conserved position — exactly the reward direction.
Ile10 is hydrophobic and likely partially buried; placing Asp at this position introduces an energetically unfavorable buried charge.
Hydrophobic-to-charged substitution near the N-terminus as a destabilizing alternative.
Charge burial of Asp at a conserved Ile is chemically destabilizing and unseen in MSA, but MPNN tolerates it (z=0.754), lowering confidence.
Tyr34 is a bulky aromatic in a hydrophobic cluster; proline substitution removes packing interactions and disrupts backbone conformation.
Tyr-to-Pro adjacent to P35 may disrupt but effect is uncertain given local proline context.
Pro occurs at 36% frequency among homologs and MPNN penalty is only moderate — position naturally tolerates proline.

rejection.reason: Pro occurs at 36% frequency among homologs and MPNN penalty is only moderate — position naturally tolerates proline.

history.rationale: Leu55 follows a glycine-rich linker and likely anchors a structural element; proline substitution should distort local fold geometry.
C-terminal Leu-to-Pro destabilizer, lower priority given C-terminal location.
MPNN finds proline nearly neutral (z=0.753), so this likely fails the disruption objective.
